business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition; primary legislation and codified statutes; no binding precedent)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU-United Arab Emirates Bilateral Investment Treaty (2004)
Luxembourg-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union FCN Treaty (1962 framework)
Luxembourg active DTA network of 92+ jurisdictions following the OECD Model, including Germany, France, Belgium, Netherlands, UK, Singapore, Mauritius, UAE and Malta

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 (transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843); CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; CSSF Circular 21/807; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 8 January 2019 on the operational modality of the RBE; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1013 and the AML/CFT framework aligned with Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 of the CJEU (22 November 2022) restricting public UBO register access.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE access restricted to competent authorities, AML/CFT obliged entities performing due diligence, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest post-CJEU C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each director, statutory manager and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) for non-EU issuing states; notarial certification is sufficient for EU/EEA documents; consular legalization required only for non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of each managing director and UBO, dated less than 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice / national criminal records bureau of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a Hague member; otherwise full consular legalization through the Luxembourg/Belgian embassy; certified French or English translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds attestation for each subscribing shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating licensed credit institution of the shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer plus Hague Apostille if the bank is located outside the EU/EEA; CSSF-compliant enhanced due diligence attestation where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and manager (utility bill or recent bank statement, not older than 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification; Hague Apostille applied for non-EU/EEA origin; sworn French, German or Luxembourgish translation attached

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence / good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or chamber of commerce in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the jurisdiction of issuance; certified French or English translation required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, statutory managers, shareholders and UBOs against the UN Consolidated List, EU CFSP Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UK OFSI list, and the CSSF/CRF (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) public warnings; automated watch-list re-screening at 30-day intervals for the first 12 months post-incorporation; PEP determination includes domestic and foreign PEPs, senior officials of international organizations and their family/closely-associated persons; enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth documentation and a 3-year cooling-off period applied for out-of-function PEPs; any match against sanctions lists triggers a mandatory freeze assessment and filing with the Luxembourg FIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Electronic Register of Companies and Commercial Register (e-RCS) - www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Latin script and may be constituted in one or more of the official languages (French, German, Luxembourgish) or in any language using the Latin alphabet subject to transliteration rules; a transliteration into a recognized official language must be included on the deed if the name is non-Latin; the legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' must appear in the deed and the published extract; the LBR rejects names containing characters outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, apostrophe, hyphen and spaces.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Etablissement de Crédit (requires CSSF banking licence)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires CAA insurance licence)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Marché Financier (regulated operator status required)
SICAV / SICAF / SICAR / Fonds / OPC / FCP (regulated investment fund lexicon)
Luxembourg / État / Grand-Duché / Administration / Commune (state or public-body affiliation requiring ministerial authorization)
Fiduciaire / Audit / Réviseur / Expert-Comptable (regulated professional titles requiring IRE/OEC approval)
Chambre de Commerce / Chambre des Métiers / Ordre (protected institutional denominations)
Names contrary to public order, morality or likely to mislead the public as to the true business object
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the application for the LBR certificate of non-objection: (1) within 5 business days file an online re-application with a written memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from the prior registered names and attaching the amended articles of association; (2) if the refusal is upheld, submit an administrative review request to the Chief Registrar of Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of the notification; (3) if confirmation of refusal is maintained, institute formal proceedings by way of a petition (requête) before the 2nd Chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 1 month of receipt of the final decision, with legal representation by an avocat à la Cour being mandatory; (4) a refused name variant may be re-filed only 3 months after the final decision; (5) where the refusal relates to a sensitive token, obtain the applicable ministerial prior-approval letter and attach it to a new name-clearance application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole physical presence. A Luxembourg SARL must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg; the registered office may be supplied by a licensed domiciliation company under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, as amended, but the statutory manager must establish real operational substance at a distinct physical address (a lease-backed data-center site and, where applicable, local staff). A pure virtual address without operational premises, staff or expenditure is treated as high-risk for AML/CFT and tax residency purposes and will attract enhanced scrutiny by the RCS, AEDT and CSSF.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated low risk of approximately 5-10% cumulative probability over a 24-month period where the registered office is supported by a genuine, lease-backed data-center site with verifiable equipment and utility contracts; the probability rises to above 70% within the same period if the company relies exclusively on a virtual domiciliation address and lacks employees, operating leases and local expenditure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance - issuance of the LBR certificate of non-objection and prior-rights screening against the RCS register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official procedure free of charge; no statutory tariff; standard processing time of 3-5 business days

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC due diligence and UBO piercing - certified background checks, criminal-record verification, PEP and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, RBE cross-checks and adverse-media review for 2-3 UBOs and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Professional services firm / legal due diligence provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark of EUR 1,500-2,000 all-inclusive for a standard SARL with non-resident UBOs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary public fee - drafting and authentication of the deed of incorporation, articles of association (statutes) and the notarial certificate of finality
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg / appointed notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial scale tariff plus drafting overhead; market all-in rate for a standard SARL ranges EUR 1,400-2,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Droit d'apport - proportional registration duty on the subscribed share capital (0.5%)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory rate of 0.5% of subscribed capital, subject to EUR 50 minimum, calculated on the EUR 12,000 proposed share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation registration fee - online filing of the deed and statutes with the Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR tariff for the online incorporation registration, approximately EUR 24

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official publication tariff of approximately EUR 100, excluding VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle - processing of passport copies, police clearances, bank references and shareholder certificates from multiple jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of the issuing states (Apostille offices) and Luxembourg embassy where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 20-50 per document for apostille plus international courier and processing fees; consular legalization charged per document where a non-Hague jurisdiction is involved

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of corporate documents into French (deed, statutes, corporate extracts and UBO evidence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of EUR 150-250 per hour; fixed fee for a combined translation pack of approximately 15-20 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening and blocked capital deposit attestation - pre-incorporation bank clearance and blocked account certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market bank charge of EUR 100-400 for account opening and issuance of the capital lock-in attestation (attestation de blocage de fonds)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Part X Articles 180-1 to 180-14 concerning Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif de société à responsabilité limitée (notarized articles of incorporation) filed electronically with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind at incorporation; cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank blocking certificate or notary escrow attestation and contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's report
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the sole founder hereby subscribes, in accordance with the draft articles of association, the full stated share capital of Société à Responsabilité Limitée to be incorporated under the corporate name (company name) — twelve thousand euros divided into (number) shares of (amount) euros each — and that payment thereof be made entirely in cash and proven by the banker's attestation. 2. That the registered office shall be established at 12, Rue des Fleurs, L-1000 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 3. That the manager(s) proposed for appointment, (full names), be and are hereby appointed as manager(s) with authority to represent the company to third parties. 4. That all required steps for incorporation, registration, publication, and administrative formalities be finalized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit subscription capital and obtain blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Luxembourg credit institution or Luxembourg notary's escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the founder's name or under the proposed corporate name, deposit at least EUR 12,000 for the SARL's share subscription, and request an attestation de blocage of the funds. The certificate must state the account holder, the amount, the deposit date and that the funds remain blocked until the company is incorporated and registered.
required_dossiers: Fully signed draft articles of association
Proof of identity of each founder
Proof of residential address
KYC/AML declaration
Power of attorney if a representative acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or notary queries the funding source, submit certified bank statements, gift declarations or loan agreements and provide a written explanation of the source of funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg (Luxembourg civil law notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Bring the draft articles and supporting documents to the chosen notary. The notary will perform identity and AML verification under the amended Law of 18 February 2004, review the corporate name, capital, registered office, managers and corporate purpose, and execute the authentic act of incorporation in the presence of the founders. The notary then transmits the deed to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Capital blocking certificate
Passport or national identity card of each founder and manager
Proof of address for manager(s)
Draft articles of association
Certificate of non-bankruptcy and good conduct for each manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires additional KYC or corporate information, furnish the requested documents and schedule a second execution appointment within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, electronic filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated notarial deed, the bank blocking certificate, proof of registered office address, manager consents and the prescribed RCS electronic forms through the LBR e-filing portal or via the notary's eDesk. The RCS will assign the registration number and issue the certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Authentic deed of incorporation
Bank attestation of capital blockage
Consent of the owner of the registered office and lease/use agreement
Manager appointment acceptance forms
RCS electronic forms A, B and C
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, correct the identified inconsistency in the electronic filing or submit an explanatory letter; resubmission is processed within 2 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish in the electronic legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, pay the publication fee and file the mandatory legal disclosure containing the company name, legal form, registered office, incorporation date, corporate object, subscribed capital and managers. Publication in the RESA makes the incorporation effective vis-à-vis third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate or extract
Proof of payment of the RESA publication fee
List of managers and their powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is refused or delayed, verify the corporate name is sufficiently distinctive and align the published particulars exactly with the RCS extract, then resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish statutory corporate books and complete officer filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS certificate has been obtained, order the share certificates, register the shareholders and share allocations in the share ledger, open the statutory minutes register, adopt the financial year, and file any final manager appointment notifications. The registered office lease term must be evidenced and kept at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Register of shareholders with share allocations
Manager acceptance form and residential authorization for third-country nationals
Registered office lease or sublease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account opening or manager background verification is pending, obtain a temporary RCS extract and file a formal undertaking to provide the outstanding clearance within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for Industry, New Technologies and Research
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated sectoral operating licence is imposed for passive server rack colocation and bare-metal hosting; a telecommunications network/service notification to the Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation (ILR) applies only if the operator offers retail electronic communications services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration as a classified establishment for backup diesel generators and refrigerating installations; no full EIA report is required for colocation operations below the prescribed building surface threshold
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the amended environmental impact assessment law and the waste and water management regulations: wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must respect municipal pH, temperature and pollutant ceilings; backup generator exhaust must meet the national air emission limits for particulate matter, NOx and CO; cooling water discharge temperature must not exceed 25°C at the point of entry into the receiving water body

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS), structural load inspection certificate from an approved Luxembourg engineering bureau, and occupational safety clearance for workers and equipment from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT/TVA registration; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax. Primary digital portal: MyGuichet.lu and impotsdirects.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities are not automatically registered for Luxembourg tax. For VAT/TVA, a non-established taxable person must file VAT registration form (Formulaire 5100 / registration request) with the AEDT, either directly when established in the EU or through an appointed Luxembourg-based tax representative when established outside the EU. Independent professionals with Luxembourg e-ID may file via MyGuichet.lu. The Luxembourg VAT ID is issued in the format LU followed by eight digits. A Luxembourg SARL receives a national identification number (matricule/NIF) at company incorporation from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and is automatically registered with the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. A foreign branch or permanent establishment must obtain its own NIF via the RCS and register with the ACD separately.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Luxembourg law provides limited elections: (i) group taxation (intégration fiscale) for resident companies that are at least 95% held by another Luxembourg resident company; (ii) VAT grouping for closely connected Luxembourg entities with financial, economic, and organisational ties; (iii) optional hybrid mismatch treatment for foreign hybrids under ATAD, including alignment of country-of-origin treatment; (iv) election for the Luxembourg permanent establishment to compute taxable profits under Luxembourg accounting rules; (v) standard EU VAT reverse-charge election for cross-border B2B supplies by non-established suppliers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA) - EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover threshold for the Luxembourg small business VAT exemption (resident established persons); no registration threshold for non-established foreign suppliers supplying taxable goods/services in Luxembourg; intra-Community distance-selling threshold of EUR 35,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate for domestic B2B/B2C VAT in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is mandatory for B2G transactions via the PEPPOL network or a Luxembourg-compliant e-invoicing platform. Tax invoices must include all EU VAT Directive details and must be submitted on the VAT return in aggregate. VAT returns and EC Sales Lists must be filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu or the AEDT e-space; no prior digital clearance of individual invoices by the tax authority is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available only to taxable persons established in Luxembourg or acting through a Luxembourg registered branch, for three categories: (i) export of goods physically leaving the EU within a maximum period of three months after dispatch, with transport verified by appropriate documentation; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-registered customer in another EU Member State, subject to a valid EU VAT number and EC Sales List requirements; (iii) supplies of services directly connected to exported goods, or B2B services where the place of supply is located in a non-EU jurisdiction. For data-center colocation, the characterization must be evaluated: if the supply is classified as leasing of immovable property situated in Luxembourg, it remains taxable at standard rate; if the supply is classified as data-center hosting/electronically supplied services to a non-EU established customer, zero-rating may apply provided the supplier holds sufficient commercial and documentary evidence that the customer belongs outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD, ENS declaration, or the official electronic export filing accepted by Luxembourg Customs and Excise)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent transport document evidencing physical departure of goods from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate - in Luxembourg practice, bank or payment-confirmation documentation (SWIFT, bank transfer, or foreign exchange record) showing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax and customs authorities may require the exporter to demonstrate, within audit, that the correct documentation was obtained at the time of supply and that the goods/services physically left the EU. Failure to substantiate a zero-rated export triggers immediate VAT assessment at the standard rate (17%) plus default interest at the statutory rate, late-payment surcharges, and administrative fines up to EUR 4,000 per irregularity. In cases of knowingly false zero-rating declarations or artificial export arrangements, Luxembourg law provides criminal penalties for tax fraud, including fines up to EUR 25,000 and/or imprisonment, plus a clawback period extended to ten years. The 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation benchmark is applied in Luxembourg administration as a banking and audit indicator; continued non-repatriation beyond 180 days without valid justification may be treated as evidence that an export transaction was not genuinely performed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) - Luxembourg's central bank and member of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); the BCL administers the national balance-of-payments statistics gateway and collects direct investment declarations through resident credit institutions; banking and payment-institution conduct, AML/CFT supervision, and sanctions-compliance enforcement are overseen by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the Luxembourg framework contains no separate foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control agency, as monetary policy and euro liquidity are managed by the Eurosystem.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg. Both the current account and the capital account are liberalised under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2003 on the free movement of capital. No BCL approval, exchange licence, or prior authorisation is required for cross-border payments, foreign direct investment, dividend repatriation, or loan repayments. The sole substantive restrictions are EU restrictive measures (financial sanctions and asset freezes) and Luxembourg implementing regulations, which typically do not apply to a compliant data centre colocation SARL. Profit remittance from the SARL is not subject to any FX permit or convertibility hurdle; the only statutory limitation is the corporate-law distributability test (the SARL must satisfy the liquidity and net-asset tests under the Law of 10 August 1915), and outbound dividends are subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where a qualifying 10% participation is held, or further reduced under applicable bilateral tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable - Luxembourg imposes no obligation to surrender, repatriate, or convert export or service proceeds into euros. Receipts from colocation, rack space leasing, bare-metal server hosting, and related services may be held in EUR or any freely chosen foreign currency. The only compliance requirement is statistical: Luxembourg resident banks and the SARL's treasury operations must record cross-border payments in the BCL balance-of-payments statistical framework, with classification under the services / telecommunication, computer, and information services category (EBOPS computer services) and, where applicable, direct investment financial flows; reporting frequency is typically monthly or quarterly through the resident clearing bank, with no approval or conversion mandate attached.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.cross_border_fx_controls_and_sanctions_r: Given the data-centre leasing model, the principal FX-relevant risk is not convertibility but sanctions screening: a Luxembourg SARL contracting with non-EU cloud-service providers, hardware vendors, or subtenants must screen counterparties, end customers, and beneficial owners against EU restrictive measures, the consolidated UN/EU sanctions lists, and CSSF guidance. Treasury instructions must include sanctions-verification clauses and wire-message sanctions screening; banks may reject or block an MT103 or SEPA payment if the stated purpose or beneficiary appears within a transaction network tied to a prohibited jurisdiction, including Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and the Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk region.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.balance_of_payments_statistical_duty: Resident banking partners file BCL statistical declarations on the SARL's behalf for inward equity injections, inbound and outbound intercompany loans, trade-related cross-border payments, and lease receivables from abroad. The treasury blueprint must ensure that every cross-border wire bears an accurate purpose code or free-text narrative, and that the SARL's accounting system can match wire references to underlying invoices and contracts, so that BCL/CSSF inspectors and the bank's compliance function can reconcile flows without triggering enhanced due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.eurosystem_liquidity_and_target2_integra: As a euro-area treasury, the SARL has unrestricted access to TARGET2 settlement and SEPA clearing through its Luxembourg bank. There is no capital-import deposit requirement, no repatriation tax clearance certificate, and no requirement to demonetise export receivables through the BCL. The legal tender status of the euro and the absence of a Luxembourg central FX desk materially reduce treasury friction for a data centre colocation business that invoices predominantly in EUR and occasionally receives USD for cross-border hosting contracts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.regulatory_authority_governing_payment_i: The CSSF regulates Luxembourg payment services under the amended Law of 1 August 2018 (implementation of PSD2), the Law of 9 November 2004 on money laundering, and CSSF Regulation 12-02. These rules govern banking account opening, remote identification, wire-transfer transparency, and AML/CFT obligations. The BCL provides the statistical reporting layer and the LMA (Luxembourg Monitoring Agency) not required for this business; the treasury blueprint should nonetheless designate a named compliance officer in Luxembourg who can sign CSSF and bank questionnaires with legal effect.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus multi-currency EUR/USD, e-banking and corporate cards
Operational Account and Capital Sewing / Escrow Account (compte séquestre) for customer security deposits
Operational Account, Treasury Settlement Account, SWIFT Corporate Access

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE - Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Scarce-Return Escrow; state-owned institution with conservative compliance appetite
Transactional Banking Account and mid-cap corporate facilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: UBS Europe SE, Luxembourg Branch (or alternative large euro-zone bank with Luxembourg branch)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Trust and Settlement Account for cross-border investor flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as the primary banking rail; MEDIUM as a supplementary disbursement rail. Luxembourg FinTech or payment institutions holding a CSSF EMI licence (under the Law of 1 August 2018) and e-money institutions authorised in another EEA Member State may operate in Luxembourg under passporting, but these entities do not hold a banking licence and cannot provide BCL statistical reporting, capital-escrow custody, commercial-letter-of-credit confirmation, or full-scope FX derivatives in the way a credit institution can. A data centre colocation SARL should not rely on a non-Luxembourg EMI (e.g., UK Finance, Revolut Business, or Airwallex) as the principal operating bank because of correspondent-bank restrictions and because the CSSF and the RBE framework require a clear, regulated local banking nexus for customer security deposits and lease-invoice collections. Digital EMIs can, however, serve as an execution-only rail for small vendor payments overseas once the main current account with a tier-1 bank is opened.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Luxembourg banks require a face-to-face or video-identified meeting with the SARL's gérant (manager) and ultimate beneficial owners. Luxembourg AML/CFT law permits remote identification under CSSF guidance only when the bank uses a CSSF-recognised electronic identification solution that satisfies the legal certainty, reliability, and wear-resistant criteria; in ordinary commercial banking, the standard is a physical interview at the bank's Luxembourg office or, for foreign-held SARLs, an interview at a bank branch/correspondent combined with notarised certified copies. The capital-subscription act for an SARL requires a Luxembourg notary to witness signatures, and the notary must in person verify the identity of the subscribing persons. Consequently, at least one director/gérant and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) should expect to appear physically before the notary and, at the bank's discretion, before the relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity - ultimate beneficial owner undisclosed or hidden behind iterative shareholding structures, trusts, or foundations in third countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); notarised articles of association; complete chain-of-ownership diagram to natural persons; passport copies of each natural-person UBO; declaration of the source of funds and source of wealth signed by the parent group; confirmation that the UBOs are not politically exposed persons, or if they are, a regulatory compliant PEP declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business pattern inconsistency - an asset-light SARL engaged in data centre colocation leasing with large lease obligations and no immediately visible technical staff
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master colocation lease or sublease agreements; contracts with Tier-3/4 data-centre operators; written business plan and 24-month projected cash flow; evidence of rack-rent fee schedules; invoices and bank statements from previous month(s) of operation; proof of technical subcontractor arrangements and facilities-management agreements; certificate of registration for Luxembourg corporate income tax, net wealth tax, and VAT (RCXML/Numéro d'identification).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA inbound capital injection - equity subscribed by parent companies in Asia, the Americas, or offshore financial centres triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the ultimate parent; bank reference letter for the parent's own account; incorporation certificates with apostille and certified translation; foreign counsel legal opinion on the parent's capacity and on sanctions absence; signed declaration of absence of underlying criminal money; evidence that the capital is allocated exclusively to colocation infrastructure deposits, rack pre-payments, and operating working capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-tripping or immediate externalisation risk - funds in-bound from the overseas parent are immediately out-bound to the same or a related home-country service provider, mimicking cash parking or layering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed liquidity forecast; treasury implementation schedule; proof of Luxembourg substance (registered seat, managing director, notified bank signatories with Luxembourg authority); service agreements and transfer-pricing documentation showing arm's-length pricing; invoices matched to delivery and usage; quarterly board minutes demonstrating operational control in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire-purpose coding mismatches and sanctions-nexus flags - payments referencing goods or services to or from high-risk jurisdictions or vague narratives
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-populated SWIFT purpose-code taxonomy of the bank (e.g., equity subscription, services paid, lease rental); evidence that counterparties clear sanctions filtering; EU/UN sanctions screening log; where needed, request to the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance or an employment of funds opinion from local counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undetermined source of customer prepayments or security deposits - colocation customers remitting QR-code or third-party payments inconsistent with the SARL's bank profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed colocation service agreement mapping each customer to a dedicated invoice; quality assurance on the customer's KYC (passport, register extract where corporate); bank reference from the customer's institution (if large); reconciliation schedule; standard terms and data-protection proof under GDPR.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.bank_account_structure_recommendation: Maintain at least two tier-1 Luxembourg accounts to mitigate bank discontinuity risk: (a) an operational EUR account with BGL BNP Paribas or SOCGEN Luxembourg collecting rack-leasing and hosting revenue and funding payroll and operating expenses; and (b) a treasury-governed account with BIL or BCEE holding customer security deposits in segregated escrow and serving as the entry point for equity injections. For the stage-4 blueprint, the account class for customer deposits should be a segregated escrow (compte séquestre) that is never commingled with working capital; this requirement is voluntarily adopted because the Luxembourg data-centre market practice treats security deposits as restricted cash, not as convertible treasury assets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the LU_SARL must execute in the following compliant sequence: (1) the SARL convenes and passes a shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase and, if applicable, a non-monetary contribution; (2) a Luxembourg notary authenticates the capital-subscription deed (acte authentique d'apport en capital) and completes the RCS filing; (3) the parent or investor remits the funds by SWIFT wire (MT103) or, for EUR within the SEPA zone, by SEPA Credit Transfer from a corporate account; the wire's purpose text must state 'Subscription of Share Capital / Capital Injection' and the SARL's RCS number; (4) the Luxembourg bank records the BCL direct-investment statistical declaration using the inward direct investment category and the underlying enterprise code; (5) upon receipt, the bank credits the escrowed capital account or designated operational account, and the SARL simultaneously updates the RBE and maintains an audit trail from the notarial deed to the bank confirmation. The funds must be verifiable as originating from the known UBO's or the documented institutional investor's own account; third-party payer financing or anonymous shareholder loans should be avoided because they create a high likelihood of enhanced due diligence requests.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments shall use the following clearing rails: (a) for EUR payments inside the EEA, SEPA Credit Transfer executed via TARGET2 settlement; (b) for non-EUR payments (USD, GBP, CHF) and EUR payments to correspondents outside EEA, SWIFT MT103 with field 70 purpose coding aligned to the BCL statistical categories, e.g., 'Software and data-centre services', 'Subsequent lease rentals / colocation fee', or 'PT capital repayment of shareholder loan'; (c) for significant equipment purchases (power distribution units, cooling systems, servers, generators) from non-EU vendors, an irrevocable Documentary Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Luxembourg bank through an advising bank, governed by ICC UCP 600 and SWIFT MT700, with the SARL as applicant and the vendor as beneficiary; (d) for related-party outflows, the payment file must be accompanied by a transfer-pricing justification (methodology, benchmark and functions, assets, risks) to prevent reclassification by the Luxembourg tax authorities and to support the bank's 'corporate payments' compliance monologue; and (e) daily treasury files are released only after positive sanctions screening and verification against the approved payment calendar.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) against a CSSF-supervised Luxembourg or EEA credit institution, with underlying exposure from future USD hosting royalties or lease payments, subject to normal counterparty credit limits and EMIR reporting/daily valuation
FX swaps (swap de change) used for short-term conversion and re-conversion of cash balances where the SARL temporarily holds USD collections while maintaining EUR-denominated operating costs

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge the currency mismatch between USD-indexed colocation receivables and EUR-denominated debt service, if the treasury committee approves a rolling hedge programme
Plain vanilla EUR/USD European-style FX options purchased (premium-pay) to protect budget conversion rates on known large capex disbursements to US-based server-equipment vendors

Commercially standard EUR/USD Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible under Luxembourg law and EMIR where the counterparty is an eligible financial institution and the reference currency is an inconvertible third-country currency; however, for the euro-based SARL they are unnecessary and should be avoided because EUR/USD is a fully deliverable market, and adopting an NDF unnecessarily creates pricing, collateral, and legal complexity.

Forward rate agreements and short-term money-market deposits are not FX hedges but are permissible liquidity instruments if the bank provides them and if they are duly recorded in the treasury statement.

Currency swap forward legs can be rolled periodically under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a CSDG/CSA (Luxembourg law collateral arrangement) only when the exact quantum of the exposure is documented.

Any derivative strategy involving leverage, exotic barrier options, or the use of embedded leverage in the SARL's treasury is prohibited; a data centre colocation business must maintain absolutely no speculative derivative profile, and all positions must be designated as cash-flow hedges under IFRS 9 with hedge documentation prepared before execution.
stage_4.liquidity_clearing_rails_detail: Monthly lease receivables from data centre colocation customers shall be collected via SEPA Direct Debit (SDD) Core or Business-to-Business (B2B) in EUR, providing deterministic settlement through the SEPA Clearer; for cross-border customers invoicing in USD, collection shall be done through SWIFT MT103 inbound wires referencing the invoice number and the customer's contract. For availability: maintain an intraday balance buffer equal to one week of the SARL's cash expenses at the principal bank. For settlement without daylight overdraft, use TARGET2 facilities through the principal Luxembourg credit institution only where a credit line has been contractually secured; otherwise disburse against confirmed balances.
stage_4.purpose_code_and_reference_data_governan: The SARL must establish an internal chart of compliant bank purpose codes that mirrors the BCL BПP classification; the blueprinted codes are: 'P1 Equity Capital Subscription' for inbound equity; 'P2 Services - Computer and Information Services' for colocation and hosting fees; 'P3 Lease/Rental of Machinery, Equipment and EDP' for rack-space leasing fees paid to data-centre landlords; 'P4 Interest on Intercompany Loans' and 'P5 Principal Repayment of Intercompany Loans' for shareholder-loan flows; and 'PG General Operating Expenses' for abroad disbursements. Every SWIFT narrative must be unambiguous, against the actual invoice, and fully consistent with the VAT and tax records of the SARL.
stage_4.bank_relationship_governance_and_account: The treasury is held under a dual-signatory matrix: the managing director (gérant) and a second authorised signatory, ideally the Chief Financial Officer or a Luxembourg-based director, must co-sign every wire above EUR 25,000. The signing mandate must be explicitly notified to the bank as an exclusive list, with no single-signatory authority for payments outside the SEPA zone. The bank mandate file shall contain a certified copy of the SARL's incorporation deeds and the gérant's identity; any power of attorney granted to a fiduciary or corporate service provider must be limited in scope and time, with a copy filed with banned third parties.
stage_4.escalation_controls_and_cssf_aml_integra: Tailored approval thresholds apply to HSBC risk cases or changes in the customer's contractual counterparties. A payment outside the pre-approved treasury calendar requires the approval of the compliance officer; any remittance to a non-OECD country to a country on the EU greylist/blacklist is subject to a standalone memorandum of the facts, a sanctions look-through, and if accepted, a legal opinion. The SARL's AML/CFT compliance function must keep bank-side KYC files updated at least annually and whenever the customer base, investors, or beneficial owners change by more than 10% of share capital.
stage_4.treasury_operating_risk_framework: The blueprint is embedded in an enterprise-wide treasury policy adopted by the SARL's board, which prohibits the use of crypto-assets, digital token settlements, or private ETF clearing for accounts payable/receivables, requires a bank counterparty rating of at least A- (S&P / Fitch equivalent) for any bank holding funds beyond EUR 500,000, and mandates that all cross-border transactions be recorded in an ERP-generated trail with an ISO 20022-conform reference; no manual book-entry adjustments are allowed without a second treasury officer review.
stage_4.stage_4_exit_criteria_and_success_metric: The stage-4 treasury blueprint is considered compliant and complete when: (a) the SARL maintains fully active operational and escrow accounts with a tier-1 Luxembourg bank; (b) all inbound capital injections are matched to notarial deeds and BCL statistical filings; (c) outbound disbursements and receiving/invoicing rails operate under signed transfer-pricing policies; (d) all FX instruments are strictly exposure-backed, IFRS 9 hedge-accounted, and governed by collateral arrangements with no net-open risk beyond 2% of annual revenue; and (e) the bank relationship file, RBE extract, UBO declarations, and sanctions-screening evidence are reviewed quarterly by the Luxembourg directors.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT + municipal business tax ~6.75% for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit for digital assets, and participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 600 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via MyGuichet.lu or eTVA electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; extensions up to 31 December are available upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg-source income only; apply DTA provisions to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income eligible for participation exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim exemption if 10% shareholding held for at least 12 months; attach supporting documentation.
Apply treaty withholding rates; submit TRC to claim relief.
Indefinite carryforward; subject to anti-abuse rules on change of ownership.
Assessed on taxable income allocated to Luxembourg permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €250 per month (max €2,500); late payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional 10% penalty for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if 10% shareholding held for 12 months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, submit a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority and Form 500/600 with the Luxembourg tax administration; treaty rates apply automatically if conditions met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory, 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive (if 25% shareholding); Interest: 15% statutory, 0% under EU Directive (if 25% shareholding). Treaty rates vary (e.g., 5% for royalties under LU-US DTA).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File required if group consolidated turnover ≥ €50 million and entity turnover ≥ €1 million; CbC report required if group consolidated revenue ≥ €750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities engaged in geographically mobile activities; data center colocation is considered a high-risk activity requiring adequate premises, staff, and expenditure in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false documentation of cross-border transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; additional 10% penalty on evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for civil restitution of unpaid taxes and face travel bans if leaving the country with unpaid liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of economic substance (no real office, no employees, no operational activity) while claiming tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, retroactive tax assessment, and penalty of €10,000 to €100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for corporate tax debts if they knowingly operated a shell entity; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence or reporting suspicious transactions in data center leasing payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €1 million for legal entities; suspension of business license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering facilitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing for intercompany leases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 10% of the adjustment, and interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they approved non-compliant pricing; potential criminal liability for tax evasion.
